corpus.text: ProctorIQ enforces automated identity verification before exam launch. Candidates must present a valid government-issued photo ID to the webcam. The system extracts OCR data and matches facial biometrics against the ID photo with a minimum 95% facial similarity threshold. If facial matching fails after three consecutive attempts, the session triggers a Tier-2 manual proctor override.

Prior to initiating the exam timer, ProctorIQ mandates a 360-degree environment room scan. The candidate must rotate their webcam across the entire testing workspace, including beneath the desk and behind monitors. Artificial intelligence models analyze the video stream for unauthorized second screens, mobile phones, or additional individuals.

ProctorIQ continuously samples candidate microphone audio at 44.1 kHz. Background noise exceeding 65 dB for more than 3 consecutive seconds is flagged as a potential acoustic violation. Advanced acoustic models isolate vocal speech frequencies from background mechanical hums like air conditioning or fan noise.

ProctorIQ employs diarization neural networks to separate multiple speaker voices. If distinct vocal signatures or whispered conversations are detected in the testing perimeter, an immediate High Severity alert is dispatched to the monitoring dashboard, and an audio snippet is cryptographically hashed for post-exam review.

The ProctorIQ Secure Browser operates in exclusive full-screen kiosk mode. It disables operating system shortcut keys including Alt-Tab, Windows Key, Cmd-Tab, PrintScreen, and function keys. Clipboard history is cleared upon launch, and copy-paste operations between external applications and exam fields are strictly blocked.

corpus.section: Section 3.1: Virtual Machine & Remote Desktop Blocking
corpus.text: ProctorIQ inspects system hardware abstraction layers to detect virtualization software. If VMware, VirtualBox, QEMU, Hyper-V, or remote access software like AnyDesk, TeamViewer, or Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) are running, ProctorIQ halts exam launch with error code PROCTOR-VM-BLOCKED.

ProctorIQ enforces single-display testing environments. The browser queries the OS display manager via EDID. If an external secondary monitor or HDMI capture card is detected, the exam screen blanks out until the auxiliary display cable is physically disconnected.

ProctorIQ captures display frame buffers at 5 frames per second using hardware-accelerated H.264 encoding. To deter photographic leaks, an invisible steganographic watermark containing candidate ID and timestamp is dynamically tiled across the test window.

corpus.section: Section 5.0: Gaze Tracking & Head Pose Estimation
corpus.text: ProctorIQ tracks eye gaze vectors and 3D head pose orientation. Looking away from the central monitor bounds for more than 5 cumulative seconds within a 60-second window triggers a Medium Severity gaze diversion flag. Persistent downward gaze towards lap level triggers an immediate inspection request.

corpus.section: Section 5.1: Object Detection in Video Stream
corpus.text: ProctorIQ real-time computer vision models run edge inference on the candidate video feed. Bounding boxes are generated for unauthorized objects including smartphones, smartwatches, textbooks, earphones, and Bluetooth earbuds with confidence thresholds calibrated to 0.85.

corpus.section: Section 6.0: Disconnection Grace Period & Offline Caching
corpus.text: In the event of network packet loss or ISP failure, ProctorIQ activates an automated 10-minute network grace period. The candidate can continue answering pre-loaded exam items while telemetry logs and video chunks are encrypted with AES-256 and cached locally in IndexedDB storage.

When Internet connectivity is restored within the 10-minute window, ProctorIQ synchronizes cached answers and transmits backlogged telemetry. If the network is not restored before the 10-minute timeout expires, the exam session auto-submits current answers to preserve partial credit.

ProctorIQ categorizes flagged events into three distinct severity tiers: Low Severity (temporary gaze drift, brief ambient noise spike under 3s), Medium Severity (persistent gaze away from screen >5s, secondary background voice), and High Severity (unauthorized person entering room, smartphone detected, VM detected, secondary monitor).

Low severity flags generate dashboard warnings. Medium severity flags dispatch a two-way text prompt from the proctor. Accumulation of three Medium severity infractions or a single High severity infraction escalates to session suspension pending live proctor review.

ProctorIQ requires a 64-bit operating system (Windows 10/11 or macOS 12+), a minimum of 8 GB RAM, a dual-core 2.0 GHz processor, 500 MB free disk space, a functional webcam with 720p resolution at 30 fps, a working microphone, and a stable broadband connection with at least 2.0 Mbps upload bandwidth.

All biometric templates, video streams, and audio recordings collected by ProctorIQ are encrypted in transit using TLS 1.3 and encrypted at rest with AES-256 keys managed in HSM. ProctorIQ strictly complies with FERPA and GDPR regulations, automatically purging candidate biometric data 30 days after exam certification.

ProctorIQ supports approved accessibility accommodations including screen magnification software, JAWS and NVDA screen readers, extended testing durations (1.5x or 2.0x time), and ergonomic movement allowances without triggering false positive gaze flags, configured through the Institutional Admin Portal.

Live human proctors supervise up to 16 concurrent candidates via a unified matrix dashboard. Proctors can send silent warning messages, pause exam timers, initiate a live 360-degree environment re-scan, or establish secure bidirectional audio communication if anomalies arise.
